author: Associated Press
description:
Court puts end to long-running legal dispute as it rules Republican-friendly map cannot be used in November

The supreme court on Friday turned away an attempt to use a new Missouri congressional map backed by Donald Trump, putting an end to a long-running legal dispute as absentee voting is under way in the midterm elections.

The justices halted a federal appeals court ruling that would have revived the Republican-friendly map for the November elections, which will determine control of Congress. There were no noted dissents.

Continue reading...
title: Supreme court blocks Trump-backed Missouri congressional map from use in midterms

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Jane Smith reportedly used ChatGPT to edit photo to show name Trump ordered US agencies to use for Lake Ontario amid trade war with Canada

The CEO of a Michigan credit union is no longer employed there, according to the organization, after she posted on social media what appeared to be an AI-generated image of her and her family wearing sweaters emblazoned with the Donald Trump-associated words “Lake America”.

In the statement recently announcing that Jane Smith would no longer be its CEO, Family First Credit Union also apologized “for the concern, disappointment and pain this situation has caused”.

Continue reading...
title: Michigan CEO loses job after posting AI-made image of her family in ‘Lake America’ sweaters

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Alleigha Botner tells court Caleb Flynn, charged with murder of wife Ashley Flynn, sent her AI love songs

The Ohio former pastor and American Idol contestant accused of fatally shooting his wife fantasized to his then lover about killing his spouse and sent her AI-generated love songs, according to evidence presented at trial this week.

Caleb Flynn, 40, is on trial for aggravated murder in connection with the 16 February shooting death of Ashley Flynn. He also is charged with two counts of felonious assault and three counts of tampering with evidence, according to a March indictment. Flynn has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-American Idol contestant told lover he dreamed of killing wife, murder trial hears

author: Maya Yang
description:
According to report, school staff recommended event move to a more secure location weeks before Kirk was fatally shot

A new report says that Turning Point USA insisted the conservative political group’s leader Charlie Kirk speak outdoors at Utah Valley University – where he was ultimately assassinated – despite security concerns raised with his team by the school’s leaders and its police chief.

The independent report with those findings was commissioned by UVU and released on Friday. The report examined security procedures leading up to the 31-year-old’s fatal shooting on 10 September 2025 during a talk at the university’s campus in Orem, Utah.

The Associated Press contributed reporting
title: Turning Point USA knew of security concerns yet insisted Charlie Kirk speak outdoors, report says

author: Ariana Baio
description:
Investigation determined Dale Caldwell violated state ethics rules and engaged in harassing behavior

Dale Caldwell, the lieutenant governor of New Jersey, resigned from his position on Friday, after the release of a report accusing him of sexually harassing a female staffer, among other ethics violations.

New Jersey’s governor, Mikie Sherrill, announced on Friday afternoon that Caldwell had submitted his resignation to her earlier in the day.

Continue reading...
title: New Jersey lieutenant governor resigns after sexual harassment accusation

author: Associated Press
description:
Idaho officials say man found dead in a church decades ago may be tied to unsolved poisonings in Chicago area in 1982

A man found dead in an Idaho church decades ago may be connected to unsolved poisonings in 1982 in the Chicago area that were dubbed the “Tylenol murders” and ushered in child safety caps for medicines, authorities announced recently.

Detective Tim Cooper of the Ada county sheriff’s Office reopened a cold case investigation in 2019 that led authorities to identify Dr Mathew Francis Betkouski posthumously. Betkouski fatally poisoned himself with cyanide more than 40 years ago and was buried anonymously.

Continue reading...
title: Idaho cold case may be tied to unsolved 1982 Tylenol murders, authorities say

author: Diane Taylor
description:
Kent facility became dangerously overburdened after ministers halted transfers to hotels

A catalogue of failures including racism, use of force and chronic overcrowding at a Home Office processing site for people who arrive on small boat were linked to decisions made at the highest level of government, an independent inquiry has heard.

The government commissioned the Manston independent inquiry to look at problems under the Conservative government between 1 June and 22 November 2022 at the facility in Kent.

Continue reading...
title: Overcrowding and racism at Manston asylum centre linked to government decisions, inquiry hears

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Walter Moorhead, arrested on suspicion of manslaughter, murdered Santos Maria Chilel Soto, partner alleges

The partner of a Delaware woman who was shot dead by a hunter allegedly mistaking her for a deer has said the killing was “senseless” and the hunter had “no excuse”.

“I have never seen a deer with only two legs,” Minivaldo Velásquez told the Delaware public news outlet WHYY in an interview published on Thursday about the death six days earlier of Santos Maria Chilel Soto. “It doesn’t make sense – no.”

Continue reading...
title: Partner of woman killed by US hunter who allegedly mistook her for deer says death ‘no accident’

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Forecasters say storm will cause heavy rains and large waves along the coast, near communities still recovering from extreme weather

Hurricane Nolo is expected to bring potentially life-threatening and catastrophic flooding to Hawaii on Friday, affecting communities that are still recovering from devastating storms earlier this summer.

The state activated more than 230 Hawaii national guard members and closed schools ahead of the storm. Nolo is expected to move west on Saturday and not directly hit the islands, but forecasters say it will still cause heavy rainfall, as much as 25in, as well as large and damaging waves along the coast.

Continue reading...
title: Hurricane Nolo predicted to bring ‘life-threatening flooding’ to Hawaii

author: Sarah Butler
description:
Funds to help local people turn empty shops, pubs and clubs into community hubs, shared workspaces and cafes

The UK government has pledged £210m to regenerate high streets by taking boarded-up shops, pubs and clubs and turning them into shared workspaces, cafes and community hubs.

Andy Burnham said the funds would “help put power back into the hands of locals who know their area best” as part of his effort to “restore pride and bring hope back”.

Continue reading...
title: Burnham pledges extra £210m towards regenerating boarded-up high streets

author: Maya Yang
description:
The singer was set to perform at Gillette Stadium as part of his Loop tour, which faces backlash over Macklemore’s removal following his pro-Palestinian comments

Ed Sheeran’s concerts at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, have been canceled due to severe weather, adding further complication to a tour embroiled in controversy.

On Friday, Sheeran’s tour promoter, Messina Touring, said: “Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium.”

Continue reading...
title: Ed Sheeran’s concerts in Massachusetts canceled due to severe weather

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Devika Bhat; produced by Angus Neale; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description: More than 100 people were arrested at large protests against the Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s address to the UN general assembly. Susan Sarandon, Chelsea Manning and Caleb Hearon were among the famous faces arrested. Inside the assembly hall, Netanyahu faced a mass walkout as he took to the stage. Then, in an inflammatory address, he claimed Israel’s war in Gaza was the ‘opposite of a genocide’ and labelled the New York mayor, Zohran Mamdani, antisemitic. Lucy Hough speaks to UK global editor Devika Bhat – watch on YouTube – Listen to Thursday’s episode of Stateside with Kai and Carter on whether Netanyahu has lost America here
title: Protests erupt as Netanyahu gives inflammatory UN speech - The Latest

author: Leyland Cecco
description:
‘Rat-free’ Canadian province recently took a verminous hit when a dead rodent turned up in town of Bowden

For more than seven decades, residents of Alberta have shared something in common with Antarctica and the high Arctic: all locations are officially free of rats.

But on Thursday the Canadian province’s reputation as a firewall against rodent infestation took a hit when the town of Bowden announced the discovery of a
title: Alberta’s ‘rat patrol’ ramps up operations as vermin makes inroads in province

author: Ariana Baio
description:
The justice called out her colleagues in a speech she made at the UDC school of law, hours after Trump filed his latest request

US supreme court justice Ketanji Brown Jackson acknowledged serious concerns about her colleagues’ handling of emergency requests, the method Donald Trump often uses to seek approval from the court.

Jackson, one of the three liberal members of the supreme court, criticized the justices’ willingness to issue rulings via the “shadow docket”, saying it undermines the public’s faith in the judicial system.

Continue reading...
title: Ketanji Brown Jackson criticizes supreme court’s handling of emergency docket

author: Guardian staff and agencies
description:
Trump and officials claimed it combats voting by noncitizens but critics said it could disenfranchise eligible voters

The US supreme court has lifted restrictions on a controversial federal database of voters as Donald Trump seeks to impose tougher restrictions on voting ahead of November’s midterm elections.

While the president and his officials have claimed the expanded database aims to combat voting by noncitizens, critics contend it could disenfranchise eligible voters.

Continue reading...
title: US supreme court lifts restrictions on controversial voter database

author: Patrick Wintour in New York
description:
Iran’s seven-day timetable would restart nuclear talks, but will the US be willing to deliver on terms that include reining in Israel in Lebanon?

Iran’s seven-day timetable to reopen the strait of Hormuz and start talks on its nuclear programme has been pitched as a deal that could rapidly extricate Donald Trump from a political crisis but requires the US president to make difficult concessions.

In the five days left before the proposed reopening of the strait, which is expected to relieve pressure on global energy markets, Trump would need to lift Iranian asset freezes, permit Iran to export its oil and, probably most difficult of all, order Benjamin Netanyahu to end Israel’s attacks on Hezbollah in Lebanon, thus achieving the “ceasefire on all fronts”.

Continue reading...
title: Trump faces tough choices as Iran dangles deal to reopen Hormuz before US midterms

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Greg Steube’s Flafo Act would require federal agencies to obtain warrants before accessing or sharing data from networked license plate readers

A Florida Republican has introduced a bill that would bar US federal agencies from using Flock Safety’s licence plate cameras and similar systems without a warrant, amid a nationwide backlash against the surveillance company.

Greg Steube’s Facilitating Liberty and Accountability for Flock Observations (Flafo) Act, introduced on Friday, would require a judicial warrant before federal agencies could buy, operate, access or share data with networked licence plate readers. It would also make US Department of Justice grants to local police conditional on their adopting similar rules.

Continue reading...
title: Republican Florida congressman introduces bill requiring warrants for Flock Safety cameras

author: Caroline Davies and agency
description:
Kenneth Newton and Melanie James filmed themselves mocking and abusing Rubin Blount, 28, who weighed 40kg when he died

A couple convicted of murder after inflicting “deliberate cruelty” on a vulnerable 28-year-old man in their care, who at the time of his death weighed just 40kg (6st 4lb), have been jailed for life.

Rubin Blount was made to stand for long periods of time, left to lie in his own urine and forced to eat out of bins by his stepbrother Kenneth Newton and Newton’s partner, Melanie James, at a property in Tamworth, Staffordshire, Stafford crown court heard.

Continue reading...
title: Couple jailed for at least 21 years for murder of vulnerable man in their care

author: Ben Doherty in Sydney
description:
As the UN warns traditional safeguards are ‘unravelling’, Donald Trump says he will encourage, not restrain, the AI race

When the Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, sat down for an interview in the heart of Silicon Valley at the weekend he had known for two days that his was the first government known to have been attacked by a rogue AI agent.

He didn’t reveal the attack then, but he sounded a warning about the march of AI: “the risk is that AI develops in a way in which humans are no longer in control of what AI is producing.”

Continue reading...
title: OpenAI hack on Australian government reveals anxiety at heart of global artificial intelligence dilemma

author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
description:
Buses for London aims for ‘greener, safer and better-value’ service but private operators say move will not fix problems

  • London buses in decline? Why public transport is slowing to a crawl – visualised

A publicly owned company, Buses for London, will start running services in the capital next year, Transport for London has announced.

TfL said the launch was a “major milestone” in its plans to improve buses for drivers and passengers.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Major milestone’: TfL to launch new public bus operator in London

author: Petra Stock
description:
Powered by sun and wind, the uncrewed vehicle will collect data to help Australian scientists better understand how oceans absorb emissions

A small uncrewed vessel has embarked on a lap around Antarctica and may not return for months.

The seven-metre craft, which looks like a large kayak in hi-vis orange, is expected to travel about 22,000km through inhospitable waters, propelled by powerful westerly winds and energy from the sun. The journey is seven times the distance between Sydney and Perth.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Robust little’ vessel begins treacherous 22,000km journey around Antarctica in the name of climate science

author: Ima Caldwell
description:
Apartment with strange view singled out in government’s fight against deceptive ads – but real estate agent says photo is no fake

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government’s crackdown on “AI-doctored” rental listings has hit a wall, after it made an example of a supposedly manipulated ad that turned out to be a genuine photograph of a $5,000 courtyard mural of Bondi beach.

In a media release on Friday announcing protections against misleading rental ads, the state government provided a link to a property in Leichhardt, claiming it was an “AI-doctored rental listing in Sydney’s Inner West”.
title: NSW crackdown on ‘AI-doctored’ real estate listings hits mural-covered wall

author: Amy Qin with graphics by Flávio Pessoa
description:
National Center for Education Statistics, which collects critical data to guide policy on learning, was decimated after Doge canceled crucial contracts

As reading and math scores fall to their lowest point in the past quarter-century, the US now has fewer tools to understand and develop interventions for this troubling trend.

When the Trump administration took a wrecking ball to the Department of Education last year, firing nearly half of its workers and allowing the so-called “department of government efficiency” (Doge) to cancel nearly $900m in contracts, a little-known agency called the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) was among the hardest hit.
title: US math and reading test scores are at a 25-year low. Trump cut the agency that can provide answers

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Forecasters say up to 40 million people in multiple US states could be affected by the early season northeasterly storm

High winds and heavy rain were beginning to batter New England on Friday as a “significant” nor’easter, the first such storm of the fall, threatened to disrupt weekend plans for millions.

In the Pacific Ocean, meanwhile, three separate hurricanes, one threatening “catastrophic flooding”, including life-threatening flash floods, in Hawaii, were churning as a record-setting El Niño continued to amplify severe weather events on a global scale.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Significant’ nor’easter brings high winds and heavy rain to US east coast

author: Associated Press
description:
Messaging ‘very telling’, says Crump after grand jury said it found no evidence of criminal conduct in teen’s death

Civil rights attorney Ben Crump released information from a forensic examination of Nolan Wells’ cellphone as well as details of the official autopsy on Thursday, just days after a Mississippi grand jury said it found no evidence of criminal conduct in the teen’s death.

Attorneys representing the 18-year-old Black college student’s family have called for transparency, asking that the grand jury investigative materials and the official autopsy report be publicly released.

Continue reading...
title: Civil rights lawyer Ben Crump releases data from Nolan Wells’ cellphone

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Trump administration move weakens federal insurance programs – and some poor people will likely forego healthcare

  • Reader Q&A: who’s spending big on the US midterms? Our reporters take your questions

The Trump administration is removing 760,000 people enrolled in the Affordable Care Act (ACA) marketplace on allegations of fraud, officials said on Tuesday – adding to previous efforts to chip away at federally subsidized insurance programs and likely causing some of the lowest-income Americans to forego healthcare, experts said.

The US government is also investigating about 420,000 people whom they suspect of fraud, and they are putting a six-month enrollment moratorium on
title: Removal of 760,000 people from ACA marketplace could undermine US health system

author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
description:
While the US president hailed the visit as ‘great’, almost nothing of substance was achieved, which was a win for Xi

  • Key takeaways from the Trump-Xi summit in Washington

If the Beijing meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in May was the “stalemate summit”, the second round of talks between the presidents of the US and China this week seemed to give up entirely on the idea of breakthroughs.

Instead, it was dubbed a celebration of “diplotainment” rather than diplomacy, where pomp prevailed over progress, and where one of the main outcomes was the news that two giant pandas would soon be sent from China to th
title: Pomp over progress as Trump rolls out red carpet for China’s president Xi Jinping

author: Maya Yang
description:
Federal agencies told to prioritize recreational fishing and to reconsider scientific standards as well as regulations

Donald Trump’s latest fishing order is raising new concerns about US marine protections, as it directs federal agencies to prioritize recreational fishing while reconsidering the scientific standards and environmental regulations that govern American fisheries.

The National Marine Fisheries Service hailed last Thursday’s order, Restoring American Saltwater Angling and Recreation, telling the Guardian: “By addressing long-standing flaws in federal data collection, streamlining permitting, and expanding marine habitats, this action delivers long-overdue stability to America’s $1.2tn outdoor recreation economy.”

Continue reading...<
title: Trump’s executive order on recreational fishing is a ‘giveaway of fish and ocean ecosystem’, advocates warn

author: Ashifa Kassam European community affairs correspondent
description:
Critics say decree also banning burqa in schools shows Italian PM running scared ahead of next year’s vote

Rights campaigners have accused the Italian government of ramping up divisive rhetoric in an attempt to court far-right voters ahead of next year’s general election after it passed a decree aimed at capping the number of newly arrived migrants in classrooms and banning the burqa and niqab in schools.

The prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, who leads the far-right Brothers of Italy party, said her government had approved what she called “commonsense measures that do not divide but genuinely help to integrate”.

Continue reading...
title: Meloni accused of election shift to right after ’shameful’ cap on foreign children in classrooms

author: Callum Jones
description:
By Donald Trump’s telling, we’re in a US ‘golden age’. Americans may feel differently. Plus: Anger at the elite and a gunfluencer runs in Texas

  • This was originally published in The Stakes 2026, a newsletter about the midterm elections. Sign up to get it in your inbox

One of Donald Trump’s greatest talents – deployed during his time as a real estate tycoon, source and subject of tabloid gossip, reality TV protagonist, and president of the United States – is his ability to tell stories. With six weeks until the US midterm elections, he is likely to lean on this instinct more than ever.

Rarely does the US president appear more comfortable than when behind a microphone, speaking without interruption, sometimes
title: When Trump’s narrative meets voters’ realities

author: PA Media
description:
Thomas appeared at Basingstoke magistrates court on Friday after being charged with criminal damage

The far-right activist Daniel Thomas has pleaded not guilty to criminal damage after he allegedly slashed a boat in the Channel with an emergency responder on board.

Thomas, 37, of no fixed address, appeared at Basingstoke magistrates court on Friday after being charged on Thursday night. He also denied failing to disclose the pin to his phone to police, under section 53 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000.

Continue reading...
title: Daniel Thomas pleads not guilty after alleged dinghy slashing in Channel

author: Rupert Jones
description:
Government-backed help to save is aimed at working people on universal credit and pays 50p for every £1 saved over four years

Amid claims that millions are missing out, the UK government is encouraging low earners to sign up to a savings scheme that offers free cash.

Help to save is a government-backed savings account that lets people earn a bonus of 50p for every £1 they save over four years.

Continue reading...
title: Britain’s low-paid urged to sign up to savings scheme offering cash bonus

author: Matthew Weaver
description:
Superhero, who was joined by others dressed as comic book characters, retrieved stolen bag after scaling wall

A scene from the fictional comic metropolis of Gotham City played out for real in Norwich last weekend when a man dressed as Batman chased a suspected thief and recovered a woman’s stolen handbag.

Sonni Mason, 25, was attending a friend’s fancy dress party on Saturday night in a Batman costume when he witnessed a handbag being snatched after a row in a queue for a nightclub in the city.

Continue reading...
title: Pow! Man in Batman costume chases down suspected Norwich handbag thief

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Customers and jobs ‘top priority’ as company closes in on deals with Opus Broadband and investment group Octopus

  • Business live – latest updates

TalkTalk is scrambling to secure its future amid the threat of administration, closing in on deals to sell its consumer and broadband arms as it seeks to save 900 jobs.

The telecoms company said on Friday it was in the final stages of sealing deals to sell its consumer business as well as its wholesale operation, PXC.

Continue reading...
title: TalkTalk races to sell consumer and broadband arms as administration looms

author: Alexandra Topping Political correspondent
description:
Former Camden council leader’s message is clear: she’s ‘visible, committed and local’, and has been for a long time

Sagal Abdi-Wali does not want to be the prime minister. She doesn’t even want to lead her party. Labour’s candidate for Holborn and St Pancras laughs and shakes her head with unusual vigour when asked if she would like to follow in the footsteps of the last member of parliament for the constituency, Keir Starmer.

“No, no, no, no, that’s not at all, in any way, what I’m trying to do,” she says during a break in campaigning in the Primrose Hill cafe in Regent’s Park. “I’m literally trying to get through the next few weeks and trying to be the member of parliament for this constituency, and that’s all I care about.”
title: Sagal Abdi-Wali: Labour’s candidate in Starmer’s former seat zeroes in on local issues amid Green challenge

author: Krishani Dhanji
description:
Expert says Australia’s criminal laws should be clarified to determine how fault is applied to a corporation when its AI agent commits a crime

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

The federal government could change Australian laws if the current legal framework could not respond to the unprecedented OpenAI hack of Medicare, ministers have confirmed.

On Friday, the government said the review by spy agency, the Australian signals directorate, would consider whether legislative change was needed after the prime minister revealed an artificial intelligence agent developed by OpenAI ha
title: ‘Wake-up call’: Labor considers changing Australian laws after OpenAI Medicare hack

author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
description:
Email to members says money lent to a party-linked company to establish a micro distillery

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation has admitted using party funds to build a $56,000 shed on James Ashby’s private property.

Guardian Australia revealed on Monday that a company linked to One Nation – Small Batch Brewing Pty Ltd – was the purchaser of the shed o
title: One Nation admits using party funds to build $56,000 shed on James Ashby’s private property

author: Kat Wong
description:
Former NSW police officer, 31, has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington terrace in early 2024

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon “guilt-tripped” a friend into helping him fake a cancer diagnosis in the hope of explaining his erratic behaviour, months before the police officer allegedly murdered Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, a Sydney court has heard.

Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Baird, 26, and his partner, Davies, 29, with a pol
title: Beau Lamarre-Condon used friend to help fake cancer diagnosis before alleged double murder, court told

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
The marked police car was travelling with its sirens on when it hit a tree in inner-city Sydney about 1.30am on Friday

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A police officer who was killed on duty when the car she was travelling in crashed into a tree has been named as 20-year-old Mia Lay.

NSW Police said the marked police car was travelling under lights and sirens along Gibbons Street in Redfern, Sydney, when it crashed about 1.30am on Friday. The officers were responding to a reported vehicle theft at Gleb
title: NSW police officer killed ‘instantly’ after car she was travelling in crashed into tree in Redfern
